newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money jumps ahead of month-end.
newsitem.headline: German call money jumps ahead of month-end.

text.p: German overnight rates roared higher on Thursday, trading near 4.25 percent, as dealers scrambled to complete month-end obligations.
The bulk of trades was conducted around 4.25 percent on the last day of the month after rates had already nudged up towards 3.05 percent on Wednesday in anticipation of some tightness on Thursday.

Dealers explained that banks had evidently not held a sufficient amount in interest-free accounts at the Bundesbank to meet the monthly reserve requirement. Consequently Lombard borrowings would be quite high today.
Dealers predicted borrowings at the 4.50 percent Lombard rate, which had already jumped to 1.8 billion marks on Wednesday, could reach up to four billion marks today.
Banks held 42.8 billion marks at the Bundesbank on Wednesday after holding 41.3 billion marks on Tuesday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 4.32500 percent on Thursday after 3.08067 percent on Wednesday.
